definition: Anorthopia is a historical term for oblique or misdirected vision, meaning squinting. It refers to a defect in how the eyes are aligned when looking.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Anorthopia; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports “Obliquity of vision” and “squinting,” but does not explicitly define “misdirected vision.”
The packet does not explicitly state that anorthopia is a “defect in how the eyes are aligned when looking,” only that it is an “Obliquity of vision” (with a reference to “VISION (defects of)”).
Because these two substantive interpretations are not directly supported by the provided text, the definition is not fully defensible against the packet.
The phrase “misdirected vision” is an unsupported paraphrase; the packet only gives “obliquity of vision” and “squinting.”
“A defect in how the eyes are aligned when looking” goes beyond the packet and adds an anatomical explanation not stated in the source.
